findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw meat (meat patties and bacon) being stored above fresh produce (potatoes) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC moved the meat below the potatoes. Ensure that good storage order is followed, with ready-to-eat foods above raw produce, which is above raw animal proteins, with raw chicken/poultry always on the bottom.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket (Cl) was measuring at too high of a chemical concentration (bleaching out the strip). CORRECTED: PIC remade the sanitizer bucket, which tested at safe and effective concentrations of 200ppm. Discussed with PIC the importance of frequently testing that sanitizing solution concentrations are at safe and effective concentration. Ensure that chemical sanitizers are used per manufacturer’s instructions for food contact surfaces by using test strips to confirm sanitizer concentration (50-200ppm for Chlorine/Bleach).
findings.citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY. [P]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed single-service plates on the cook line counter were stored without protection from an upper shelf and were stored upright instead of inverted. CORRECTED: PIC moved plates either under a protected shelf or inverted them on the cook line counter to protect the food-contact surfaces from debris. Ensure that the food-contact surfaces of single-service articles are stored to protect them from falling debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed standing water in the bottom of the kitchen prep cooler, caused by excess condensation in the upper part of the prep cooler. Staff have been instructed to soak up the condensation with clean and dry towels, but the towels had already soaked through and water had begun pooling again. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the towels were replaced with dry towels. Inspector discussed with PIC that the cooler may need repair. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of residues and moisture.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mops were drying in the lower basin of the mop buckets instead of the upper baskets. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mops to the upper baskets, allowing them to effectively air-dry. Inspector and PIC discussed alternative methods that would allow mops to more effectively air-dry, including hang drying them above a dedicated mop sink. Ensure that mops are in a position that allows them to fully air-dry between uses.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the walk-in cooler has a persistent drip from one of the fans that is being caught below in a plastic basin. PIC and staff make sure to keep that area free of food that could become contaminated from the dripping water. PIC states that the repair person said the drip was to be expected as the humidity increases, but the drip is continuous and could easily overflow if not carefully monitored. Please repair the walk-in cooler element to prevent continuous drips and potential contamination of food. Ensure that physical equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the soda nozzle at the wait station has soil accumulation. The person in charge (PIC) was informed and he stated the nozzles would be cleaned by the close of work. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid soil or mold build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed light passing through the door by the triple sink. The PIC was informed and educated on the risk of pests entering the facility through gaps. Ensure all outer openings are sealed to prevent entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed food debris in the knife storage container. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the container was transferred to the triple sink for washing. Ensure all equipments and utensils are stored in a location free of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT - Observed the handle of the cook line freezer is in a state of disrepair. A portion of the plastic has broken off exposing the soft, absorbent material underneath. The handle must either be replaced or repaired so that the absorbent material is not exposed. Ensure that the handle is a smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent surface by the next routine inspection. PIC discussed plans to cover the inset handle and install another handle above. Ensure repairs are smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT - Inspectors observed grease build-up on the wall and floor behind the grills on the cook line. The PIC was informed, he stated cleaning is done every 4-6 months and would be cleaning those areas very soon. Ensure the wall and floor behind the grills on the cook line is cleaned before the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed gap between the wall and floor titles under the triple sink. The PIC was instructed to seal the gap so that from the wall to the floor is smooth, easily cleanable and prevents water accumulation. Ensure the gap is sealed by next routine inspection to prevent water accumulation and also a hideout location for potential insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the handle of the cookline freezer is in a state of disrepair. A portion of the plastic has broken off exposing the soft, absorbent material underneath. The handle must either be replaced or repaired so that the absorbent material is not exposed. Ensure that the handle is a smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The interior of the microwave by the kitchen entrance (near the spices/seasonings).

(2) The dust on the metal wire dish drying rack near the dish machine.

(3) The dust and other debris on the walk-in cooler fans. 

(4) The grease build-up on the wall behind the grills on the cookline. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a large bag of cooked sausage stored in a steam table unit that was turned off. The PIC stated that the sausage was taken out of the cooler about 15 minutes ago. The inspector explained they need to either: (1) Turn on the steam table and keep them above 135F; (2) Leave them inside the cooler at 41F or below; or (3) Use time-as-control (if this method is used, than the time the sausage was removed from the cooler must be written down to indicate the four hour time-as-control window). The PIC decided to put the sausages inside the cooler. There is also cooked bacon stored in the turned off steam table; however, cooked bacon is temperature stable and is allowed to remain. Ensure that foods are always stored to maintain food safety.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the cookline prep table. The employee cooking was educated and they moved the wiping cloth into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the following utensils stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination:

(1) A knife on the cookline stored with the blade in the gap in between the prep cooler and freezer. The gap is not a clean and sanitized surface so it poses the risk of contamination. The knife was moved to another location during the inspection.

(2) A knife stored with the handle in contact with cooling gyro meat shaved from the spinning spit. The knife handle is touched by bare hands and poses the risk of contamination. The knife was removed from the gyro meat during the inspection. 

(3) The sugar scoop stored with the handle in contact with the sugar. The sugar scoop handle is touched by bare hands and poses the risk of contamination. The sugar scoop was removed from the bag during the inspection. 

Ensure that utensils are always stored properly to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the shelves above the triple sink used for drying clean dishes are soiled with debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FISRT REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the caulking behind the spray nozzle table to the left of the dish machine has been removed and not replaced. The spray nozzle table must be sealed to the wall. Due to the area being subject to high amounts of moisture the caulking must be repaired/replaced frequently. Ensure that the caulking is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector immediately educated the employee when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier it always used to turn off the faucet to avoid contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee grab toast from the toaster and place it on a plate for serving with their bare hands. The PIC was immediately notified when the action was observed. The PIC stated that the facility had recently ran out of gloves and more were on order. The inspector explained the importance of immediate action to ensure a barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods. The PIC placed a pair of tongs by the toaster and another employee went to the store to purchase gloves. The employee returned with the gloves during the inspection. Ensure that gloves or another barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw hamburger meat stored above various vegetables in the right prep cooler bottom. An employee moved the raw meat below the vegetables during the inspection. The inspector explained the importance of storing raw foods underneath any ready-to eat foods to avoid contamination. Ensure that foods are always stored according to the proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sanitizer bucket under the grill was testing at 10 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. After the PIC remade the bucket it was testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector suggests increasing the frequency that sanitizer buckets are changed. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (chlorine = 50-200 ppm).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed two containers of soup in the walk-in cooler had exceeded the 7-day maximum. The soups had a date mark indicating the food was prepared on 1/20/2025 meaning it should have been discarded on 1/26/2025. The PIC was notified and the soup was discarded during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of discarding foods after 7 days (the day the food is prepared being day 1). Ensure that foods are always discarded when they exceed the 7-day maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the caulking behind the spray nozzle table to the left of the dish machine is not attached to the wall and is degrading in quality. The caulking must be removed and replaced with fresh caulking. Due to the area being subject to high amounts of moisture the caulking must be repaired/replaced frequently. Ensure the caulking is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness expired in August 2024. The PIC stated they were unaware it had expired and they will schedule a new training. No one else present at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the PIC has a certificate in allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC was instructed to educate employees on proper hand washing technique. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off faucets after hand washing to prevent re-contamination. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the front service area (coffee, dessert, and salad stations) did not have a hand washing sink. The PIC stated that employees either wash their hands in the bathroom or in the kitchen. There is a triple sink which is not being used to wash dishes in the front service area. Soap was provided to this sink to be used as a hand washing sink. There was already paper towels and an employee must wash hands before returning to work sign at the sink. Ensure the sink is used for handwashing in the front service area.

5-204.11: A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several phones stored in positions that could cause food cross contamination. Phones were stored on a shelf over the dish machine amongst clean dishes, on a towel holding clean dishes at the area where food is picked up by waitresses, and sitting on the table where food is prepped by waitresses. The PIC moved the phones during the inspection. Ensure that phones are stored away from food prep areas to protect food from cross contamination.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer bucket at the front service area was testing a 10 ppm (Cl). After the PIC added more bleach to the bucket it tested at 200 ppm. Ensure sanitization buckets have a minimum concentration of 100 ppm and are tested on a regular basis.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the microwaves beneath the shelves of seasoning had an accumulation of soil inside on the bottom, sides, and top. Soil in microwaves presents a risk of food contamination. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop being stored in a mop bucket with the head in the water. Ensure that mops are stored in a position that allows the head to air dry. The mop head was moved to a position where it can air dry during the inspection.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
